title: H177 — PEAD-RL: Hierarchical reward model for post-earnings CAR prediction
rationale: arXiv 2602.19919 (Janus-Q, Feb 2026) reports 102% Sharpe improvement and +17.5% direction accuracy using hierarchical gated reward modeling on 62,400 annotated financial news articles (10 event types, including earnings). The key idea: instead of a binary WIN/LOSE label like H172's classifier, train a hierarchical model that predicts both direction AND magnitude of post-announcement return, using RL-style reward shaping. This could fix H172's core problem (binary classifier doesn't capture return distribution shape). Dataset: their annotated 62,400 articles are available. Implementation: use their CAR-labeled training set as fine-tuning data for our FinBERT model on our 30-stock universe's IS events (n=112). Risk: HIGH effort (~20h) and requires a larger training set than our 112 IS events. Flagged for Kevin review before scheduling.
content:
New hypothesis (HIGH EFFORT — flag for Kevin review):

H177 — PEAD-RL: Hierarchical reward model for post-earnings CAR prediction

Design:
  Based on Janus-Q (arXiv:2602.19919). Instead of binary WIN/LOSE label,
  use hierarchical reward model:
  - Level 1: direction (UP/DOWN)
  - Level 2: magnitude (quintile of 20d return)
  - Reward: +1 for correct direction × magnitude weight

  Training data: Our IS 112 events + Janus-Q's public 62,400 article dataset
  (cross-domain transfer — news articles, but earn-specific subset)

  Architecture:
  FinBERT CLS embedding (768-dim)
  → Hierarchical MLP: direction head (2-class) + magnitude head (5-class)
  → Combined loss: BCE(direction) + CE(magnitude) + RL reward term

  Compare vs H172 (binary classifier, NOT CONFIRMED: WR 77.1% but MeanRet 3.37%)
  Goal: improve MeanRet from 3.37% to >= 5.5% by optimizing for return magnitude

Estimated effort: 20h
Prerequisite: Download Janus-Q dataset first
Flagged for Kevin review before starting
